public_sources.title: Blinded sample size review for McNemar's test based on primary and surrogate endpoints
public_sources.used_scope: Recent paired-binary primary source: exact McNemar conditions on discordant count; blinded sample-size adaptation based only on discordance information preserves the binomial sign law/type-I error in its tested assumptions; power depends critically on discordance rate.

public_sources.title: Curtailed versions of randomized binomial tests
public_sources.used_scope: Classical result/background: for a nonrandomized fixed-size binomial test, an optimally curtailed version can stop as soon as the final decision is mathematically certain without changing the terminal decision rule.

public_sources.title: A two-stage phase II clinical trial design with nested criteria for early stopping and efficacy
public_sources.used_scope: Operational curtailed-sampling background: stop once enough successes or failures make a stage decision certain; sample size follows a stopped-negative-binomial form.

public_sources.title: Active Sequential Hypothesis Testing with Non-Homogeneous Costs
public_sources.used_scope: Cost-aware sequential-testing background: heterogeneous observation cost changes optimal sensing/testing policy; optimize information relative to expected cost rather than a naive per-step ratio. Not used as a theorem for the paired-sign derivation.

exact_terminal_equivalence_curtailment.result: For a candidate audit whose terminal decision is commit iff W_r>=k among r discordant signs, sequentially stop as soon as either k wins have occurred (commit is now inevitable) or r-k+1 losses have occurred (commit is now impossible). This produces exactly the same terminal commit event as the fixed-r audit, so the candidate null tail probability p, alternative power a, tail-floor e-value map, lifetime FWER path, and worst-placement true-commit probability are unchanged.
exact_terminal_equivalence_curtailment.null_stopping_law: Under sign-null p_sign=1/2, P(T=t,commit)=C(t-1,k-1)2^{-t} for t=k..r and P(T=t,noncommit)=C(t-1,r-k)2^{-t} for t=r-k+1..r.
exact_terminal_equivalence_curtailment.scope_guard: Requires a pre-fixed nonrandomized terminal tail event and no use of future/unobserved outcomes. Randomized terminal tests need separate curtailment accounting.

discordance_waiting_cost_factorization.result: With a fixed per-pair discordance rate rho and sign independent of discordance waiting time, the curtailed sign process determines a distribution over total discordances R. Conditional on R, total paired observations required to see those discordances are negative-binomial NB(R,rho). Therefore the all-null pair-cost distribution of an entire candidate stream is an exact mixture over R, including false-commit stopping paths and horizon-survival paths.
discordance_waiting_cost_factorization.scope_guard: Fixed rho within a cost scenario; candidate-dependent or history-dependent rho requires a different waiting-time model.

policies.policy: r10 maximin: k10 x17 then k9 x3
r20 maximin: k17 x15 then k16 x5
r30 maximin: k24 x1 then k23 x19
r50 maximin: k36 x8 then k35 x12

current_policy_cost_recalculation.interpretation: The previously posed high-quantile cost constraint changes materially before any statistical re-optimization: exact deterministic curtailment moves the r20 maximin policy from q95=2148 pairs to q95=992 pairs at rho=.20 with identical statistical power/FWER. Thus a 1000-pair q95 budget that previously appeared to force r10-level weak audits can already accommodate the stronger r20 policy after implementing decision-equivalent curtailment.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Realize each fixed-discordant tail-floor audit as an optimally curtailed Bernoulli race, stopping when commit or noncommit is mathematically certain.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Exact terminal-event equivalence plus exact stopped-binomial/negative-binomial mixture calculation on all four existing maximin depth policies.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Nonrandomized terminal upper-tail event; fixed discordance-rate cost scenario for pair-count quantiles.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Before solving a chance-constrained statistical DP, exhaust decision-equivalent operational curtailments that lower sample cost without changing the test; optimize statistical boundaries only after this free cost reduction.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: r20 q95 at rho=.20 falls 2148->992 with exactly unchanged tested statistical operating characteristics.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Only equivalence-preserving curtailments; stochastic futility/efficacy rules that alter the terminal event require new type-I/power analysis.

rejected_or_narrowed_generalizations: Rejected: a fixed-r terminal audit must always collect all r discordant outcomes. For a nonrandomized tail event it can stop as soon as the terminal decision is certain.

Rejected: under a 1000-pair 95th-percentile budget at rho=.20, the tested r20 maximin policy is necessarily infeasible. It becomes feasible after exact curtailment (q95=992) without changing its statistical behavior.

Narrowed: shallow-to-deep screening should trade power for cost. Deterministic impossibility/inevitability curtailment is a stronger first move because it reduces cost with zero power/FWER trade-off; only after exhausting it is stochastic shallow-to-deep screening worth optimizing.
Narrowed: negative-binomial full-r cost is the relevant cost model. Under curtailment the stream induces a mixture over random total discordances R, followed by NB(R,rho) waiting cost.

frontier.action: Re-solve the constrained robust depth/boundary problem using optimally curtailed candidate tests as the base action. Sweep rho=.20 q95 budgets 300-3500 and determine the Pareto frontier of worst-position q=.60 true-commit probability versus pair-cost tail; compare fixed r with mixed r schedules.

Generalize from fixed rho to candidate/history-varying discordance rates and derive conservative pair-cost tail bounds when sign symmetry remains valid but waiting-time distributions differ across candidates.
Only after exact curtailment, test stochastic early futility/deepening rules that alter the terminal commit event; quantify their additional cost savings against power loss and lifetime FWER.
Study randomized terminal boundaries and exact curtailment/randomization interactions so discrete alpha slack can be used without breaking decision equivalence.
Measure wall-clock savings under batched/parallel rollout execution, where discordant-count savings may not translate linearly to elapsed time.

exact_next_action: Compute the exact curtailed cost-power Pareto frontier across r in {10,20,30,50} and mixed-depth schedules under rho=.20 q95 budgets from 300 to 3500 pairs, then identify where any stochastic shallow-to-deep rule can improve beyond equivalence-preserving curtailment.
